messages:
siena: Heads up — after bringing up magnet16k-int4 on the staging fleet I see a subtle context divergence for very long prefill sessions (>48k tokens). Repro is noisy but consistent on one seed.

siena: Symptoms: tokens generated mid-stream diverge from baseline FP16 run, often when a repeated anchor sequence appears near token ~50k. Looks like an off-by-one in RoPE index mapping or a bias/rescaling issue after quantized prefill.

vikram: can you paste the minimal repro and the model/commit?

siena: commit: a1c9f3d (onnx-quant int4 pass). Run used: ./run_infer --model magnet16k_int4.onnx --prefill-file long_prefill.txt --max-tokens 62000 --batch 1

siena: snippet from logs around divergence:
```
[2026-03-17 14:02:11] kv_store: prefill step 49120: write_idx=49120 shard=2
[2026-03-17 14:02:11] attn: rotary_idx=49120 scale=1.00003
[2026-03-17 14:02:11] kv_store: get_idx returned 49119 for query 49120
[2026-03-17 14:02:12] gen: output token mismatch at pos 50403 expected="the" got="a"
```

luka: interesting — get_idx off by one at the KV read. can you repro with verbose kvcache debug (index/seq ids) and attach dumps?

siena: attaching a small trace: kvcache_dump_{seed}.txt (I'll upload to the thread). It's basically a copy of key indices per layer for tokens 49000..50500.

oliver: low-effort hypothesis: int4 packing changed alignment so memcpy/stride produced shifted indices on one shard. Did quant pass change layout?

siena: quant pass did switch to 4-bit nibble packing + a reshape op earlier in the graph. We added a fast path for prefill that flattens some dims.

vikram: can you run the same prefill with the previous int8 build or FP16 and compare the kv index sequence? That will isolate whether it's quant packing or the RoPE math.

siena: ran FP16 -> no divergence. int8 (old branch) -> no divergence. int4 (new) -> reproduces.

oliver: that strongly suggests packing/layout bug. But logs show rotary_idx=49120, then get_idx returned 49119. Could be an atomic increment ordering or a fence missing when we batch-write keys across shards.

luka: Also note the scale value 1.00003 — are we applying a scale correction after quant dequant? maybe rounding drift accumulates and shifts a boundary when conversion toggles a comparison.

qa-bot: automated-regen ran on the same config 3x, reproduces 2/3 times. Seed: 42 reproduces, seed: 97 does not.

vikram: OK. Plan: 1) add assert hooks in kvcache write/read to check identity of indices (quick local build), 2) run single-shard deterministic run with logging, 3) bisect the quant pass (revert nibble reshape) to confirm. I'll take 1+2. @siena can you make a reduced prefill that still hits the window? 20-30k prefix + anchor repeat should be fine.

siena: will produce reduced test. quick note: this only appears when prefill > window_size (we set window_size=65536 >> so we do exceed that). Might also be an interaction where token index modulo window wraps differently after packing.

oliver: if it's modulo/window wrap bug, reproducer should also hit smaller windows if we shift anchor earlier. Try replicated anchor at ~30k too.

siena: reduced test made: prefill 32000 + anchor repeat at 31k/62k -> still repro. uploading reduced_prefill_31k.txt

vikram: running assert-build now. attaching debug command: 
```
BUILD_TAG=kv-assert-20260317 bazel build //runtime:inference --config=int4-assert
./bazel-bin/runtime/inference --model magnet16k_int4.onnx --prefill reduced_prefill_31k.txt --verbose-kvcache --dump-kv=kvtrace.json
```

luka: add a small check: when reading KV index i, assert stored_key_pos[layer][i]==i. If false, log surrounding indices +/-8.

vikram: good. I see one failing log already: read_idx 31017 returned key_pos 31016 on shard 1, layer 8. Surrounding snapshot: 31012..31022 shows a one-off slip at exactly where a nibble boundary crosses a 64-bit word.

oliver: that nails packing alignment hypothesis. Likely a fence or an off-by-nibble shift when copying last partial byte.

siena: any quick mitigation for staging? revert int4 nibble reshape to old layout and redeploy canary?

vikram: yes. revert patch a1c9f3d -> a1c9f3c (previous) on staging. Canary deploy now.

qa-bot: canary results: 0/5 reproductions on canary after revert.

oliver: follow-up: add unit test for nibble boundary copy (cross-platform) and add fuzz cases for windows sizes near 8/16/64 boundaries. Also add telemetry to detect kv index mismatches in production quickly (metric: kv_index_mismatch_count).

siena: I'll file a PR with reduced reproducer + test + upload kvtrace. Thanks all.

vikram: great catch. tagging for postmortem and a short blurb in rolling notes. :thumbsup:
